parsed.basis: Atlanique, centred on Cotonou, is Benin's southern coastal and most urbanised department and its economic capital, with greater anonymity, business and foreign presence than rural areas where hostility is reported as strongest. Nationally, consensual adult same-sex conduct is legal, but there is no protection based on gender identity, legal gender recognition is impossible, and LGBTI organisations cannot register. Routine refusal of hormone and general medical care, religious framing of transgender people, and civilian anti-gay lynchings described as commonplace with police rarely pursuing perpetrators apply across the country. Cotonou has hosted public gatherings and small survivor-support accommodation, yet no department-level protection distinguishes visitors from the national pattern of impunity and service denial.
